data.gender_notes: Sejad is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Sejad is derived from the Sanskrit word 'sage' or 'wise'. It is a name for a leader or a wise man. It is also associated with water and rivers, symbolizing the flow of knowledge and understanding. The name Sejad carries the meaning “Wise, Sage, Leader” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Urdu. Parents who choose Sejad usually hope their child will grow to embody wise, sage, leader and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Sejad belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wise, Sage, Leader.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sejad total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Sejad was a king of the Satavahana dynasty in the Deccan region of India, reigning from around 150 AD to 165 AD.
historical_references.context: Sejad was an important ruler during the Satavahana period, which had its roots in the Maurya Empire and lasted until the 3rd century AD. The Satavahanas were a major power in the Deccan region and controlled much of present-day Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka.

historical_references.reference: Sejad is also mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic, as a Yadava prince who was a descendant of Krishna.
historical_references.context: The Mahabharata is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, the other being the Ramayana. The epic describes the Kurukshetra War between two branches of a single royal family, the Pandavas and the Kauravas. Sejad's connection to Krishna adds historical and religious significance to his name.
